cleanIntro: Colt's own stripping procedure for the Single Action Army, then the cleaning it calls for. On this revolver the strip is one thing — the cylinder comes out — and Colt says so explicitly.

steps.title: Hammer to half-cock so the cylinder turns
steps.action: Draw the hammer back to the half-cock position. The cylinder is now free to rotate clockwise.
steps.prose: Half-cock is the working position on a Single Action Army — it is what frees the cylinder for loading, unloading and everything below.
steps.quote: Draw hammer back to Half-Cock position.
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — To Unload Revolvers With Ejector Rods, step 2, p.24
steps.warn: Always keep the muzzle pointing in a safe direction, well clear of your body, particularly when unloading.

steps.title: Open the loading gate
steps.action: Swing the loading gate open on the right side of the frame.
steps.prose: The gate exposes one chamber at a time. Nothing on this revolver is loaded or unloaded with the gate shut.
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — To Unload Revolvers With Ejector Rods, step 3, p.24

steps.title: Eject one chamber at a time, all the way round
steps.action: Keeping your fingers away from the trigger, align a chamber with the ejector rod under the barrel and push the rod backwards through the chamber to force out the round or case, then let the rod return forward under its spring. Rotate the cylinder clockwise to the next chamber and repeat until every chamber is empty.
steps.prose: Six presses, six looks. There is no swing-out cylinder here to show you the whole thing at once.
steps.caution: If a cartridge or case will not come out this way, Colt's own answer is to remove the cylinder and use the base pin to push the remaining rounds out.
steps.quote: forcing out the live round or empty case
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — To Unload Revolvers With Ejector Rods, step 4, p.24

steps.title: Confirm all six are empty
steps.action: With the hammer at half-cock and the gate open, rotate the cylinder and confirm all six chambers are empty before going any further.
steps.prose: Colt repeats this as its own numbered step at the head of the stripping section, which tells you how it expects the check to be treated.
steps.quote: Rotate cylinder and ensure all six chambers are empty.
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 4, p.32
steps.warn: ENSURE THAT THE REVOLVER IS NOT LOADED BEFORE STRIPPING AND CLEANING.

steps.title: Depress the base pin retaining catch
steps.action: Press in the base pin retaining catch, which sits on the left side of the frame in front of the cylinder.
steps.prose: It is a small spring-loaded button that engages a groove in the base pin. Until it is held in, the pin will not move at all.
steps.caution: Blackpowder-frame revolvers instead have a base pin retaining screw in front of the frame, which must be removed with a properly fitting screwdriver before the base pin will come out.
steps.quote: Depress base pin retaining catch (located on left side of frame in front of cylinder).
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — STRIPPING FOR CLEANING, step 5a, p.32

steps.title: Draw the base pin forward and out
steps.action: Keeping the retaining catch depressed, pull the base pin forward out of the frame, then release the catch.
steps.prose: Forward, toward the muzzle. The pin is the cylinder's axle and its extractor both — do not put it down where it can roll away.
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — Revolvers Without Ejector Rods, step 5b, p.26

steps.title: Roll the cylinder out to the right
steps.action: Carefully take the cylinder out to the right of the frame, avoiding contact between the ratchet and the loading gate.
steps.prose: To the right, past the open gate. The ratchet teeth on the back of the cylinder are soft enough to burr against the gate if you drag it across.
steps.caution: Take great care not to drop the cylinder — if it still holds live rounds, dropping it can fire one.
steps.quote: Carefully remove cylinder to the right of frame avoiding contact
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — Revolvers Without Ejector Rods, step 5c, p.27

steps.title: Use the base pin to clear anything stuck
steps.action: If a round or case would not eject earlier, use the base pin to push the remaining rounds out of the cylinder now that it is in your hand.
steps.prose: This is Colt's own answer to a stuck case, and it is why the base pin is worth keeping to hand rather than pocketing.
steps.quote: Use base pin to remove remaining rounds until all chambers are empty.
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — UNLOADING — Revolvers Without Ejector Rods, step 5d, p.27

steps.title: Field strip complete — the cylinder is the whole of it
steps.action: Frame with barrel and grips, cylinder, and base pin. Colt states directly that the revolver is not to be stripped further than removing the cylinder, and sends anything beyond that to Servicing and Repair.
steps.prose: It is a short list, and it is the whole list. The lockwork behind the side plate is not owner-serviceable by the manufacturer's own instruction.
steps.quote: ALWAYS LET A QUALIFIED GUNSMITH WORK ON YOUR GUN
steps.cite: Colt Single Action Army Revolver / Sheriff's and Storekeeper's Model Revolvers / New Frontier Single Action Army Revolver — Safety and Instruction Manual — ABSENT — no form or part code printed anywhere the OCR can read — SERVICING AND REPAIR, p.37
steps.warn: A collector's revolver should not be stripped for cleaning at all — Colt says it should only be wiped gently on the outside with a very soft dust-free cloth.

deepAbsentReason: Colt bounds this book inside its own stripping section: the IMPORTANT note on p.33 tells the owner not to strip the revolver further than removing the cylinder, and directs any additional maintenance to "Servicing and Repair", which in turn says to let a qualified gunsmith work on the gun. (That IMPORTANT sentence is quoted here in paraphrase rather than verbatim because the OCR of this scan breaks the word "cylinder" across a line as "cye tinder" — the sentence is legible, but it cannot be quoted verbatim without transcribing the OCR's error.) The manual publishes no procedure past cylinder removal, so this listing has NO deep clean.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Attach a cotton flannel patch to the cleaning rod, insert it at the muzzle and pass rod and patch down through the barrel; repeat, changing patches, until the last one comes out clean
Take care to avoid striking the rear frame of the revolver — Colt warns that severe cases burr the metal around the firing pin hole, which can lead to firing failures
If the barrel is still dirty after firing, scrub it with a brass wire bristle brush dipped in gun cleaning solution, passing the brush all the way through before reversing direction

cleaning.name: CYLINDER AND CHAMBERS
tasks: Clean each of the six chambers with the same rod-and-patch method used on the barrel
Scrub the chambers with the brass brush if they remain dirty, then re-patch and re-inspect
Wipe the ratchet at the rear of the cylinder and the base pin bore clean

cleaning.name: FRAME AND EXTERIOR
tasks: Clean the rear face of the barrel and the revolver frame with a small toothbrush
Lightly moisten a flannel patch with gun oil and pass it once through the barrel and each chamber, leaving a thin film for storage — or pass a dry patch through if the revolver is going back into use
Check no flannel or brush bristles have lodged anywhere, then wipe all external surfaces with an oil-moistened patch

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Clean as soon after firing as possible — the job is easier and there is less chance for corrosion to start
Unfired, clean it once or twice a year in a temperate climate, or as often as once a month in a tropical one
If you carry it loaded, unload it and clean it at least once a month; if it gets wet, clean it as soon as possible
Below freezing, avoid oil and apply a dry lubricant sparingly instead

reassembly: With the hammer at half-cock, roll the cylinder back into the frame from the right side, keeping the ratchet clear of the loading gate.
Install the base pin and secure it — on a blackpowder frame, refit and tighten the base pin retaining screw.
Check that the cylinder rotates freely.
Lower the hammer to the safety position and close the gate.
fncheck: With the revolver empty and the gate closed, cock the hammer through a full rotation and confirm the cylinder indexes and locks on each chamber — the bolt should be heard clicking into the cylinder notch. Then lower the hammer into the safety position under thumb control: draw it back slightly, squeeze the trigger only long enough for the hammer to clear the half-cock notch, release the trigger completely so the safety notch can engage, and ease the hammer down.
